title: 🔴  Cómo tener RITMO en la SALSA | ¡Te explico muy sencillo! ✅

method.teacher_system: The teacher introduces different ways to count salsa and explain song structure. She plays popular salsa tracks to demonstrate listening for the repeating musical phrase to find the one. Then she guides learners to listen for specific percussion like the tumbadora to locate beats four and eight.
method.signature: Using a phone to play real salsa tracks while explaining how to listen for specific instruments on screen.

practices.what: Listen to the song Tihuanaco to identify the repeating musical phrase that marks the one.
Listen to Y no hago más na to identify the tumbadora double hit marking four and eight.
Listen to Soledad by Sonora Ponceña to practice finding the beat in a different salsa track.
Listen to Ojos chinos by Gran Combo to identify the bell accent marking odd numbers.
Listen to Arroz con habichuelas to discuss the clave and how it relates to the beat.

beliefs.belief: The teacher believes that learning is a process of sharing practical exercises that have worked for others.
It is completely fine if you cannot follow every count right away as long as you find the one.
There can be controversies between dancers and musicians regarding the clave, but beginners should focus on simple listening.

feelings.response: The teacher simplifies the task by telling the learner to ignore instrument names and just focus on the repeating sound.
The teacher validates the learner's struggle by saying it is okay not to get the full count right away.

moments.says: The teacher introduces the topic of finding the rhythm in salsa music, emphasizing that the lesson is about listening rather than dancing.
The teacher clarifies that she is not a professional musician and that these exercises are simply what she uses with her students.
The teacher encourages the learner to focus on the repeating sound or phrase in the music to identify the beat.
The teacher reassures the learner that it is okay if they cannot follow the entire count yet, as long as they can identify the one.
The teacher celebrates that the learner has made significant progress by identifying the four and eight beats.
The teacher encourages the learner to practice identifying the beat in any salsa song they listen to from now on.

mentor.what_stays: The teacher leaves the learner feeling capable and encouraged to trust their own ability to hear the rhythm in music.

struggles.theme: Struggling to find the rhythm for decades
Hearing the music in black and white without feeling the beat
Getting distracted by looking at the teacher instead of listening
Confusing which instrument marks the beats
Having only one leg and needing to repeat the video many times

clicked.theme: Learning that the tumbadora marks four and eight instead of one and five
Finally understanding how to find time one when the musical phrase repeats
The color dot editing on screen is extremely helpful

requests.theme: Requesting a similar tutorial for bachata
Requesting a video where the teacher moves while explaining the rhythm
Wanting to hear about the debate between musicians and dancers regarding times

meant.theme: Providing the best explanation found after struggling for years
Giving hope to finally be able to dance salsa
Unlocking a musical brain for salsa

method.limits: The video is a seated talking-head tutorial focusing on listening to music samples rather than physical dance steps.
